title: Gale Force 5 rides 225 miles for cancer research - Bristol Myers Squibb
summary: More than 325 Bristol Myers Squibb employees from over 30 markets will ride nearly 6,000 miles across four continents in 2026, coming together through C2C4C to support cancer research worldwide.
body_markdown:
**Jerome Lebrun, vice president, Commercial Procurement**


Behind every rider is a list of names. For Jerome, those names are Jacques, Ramon, Javi and many other relatives in his life who have been touched by cancer over the years. "Jacques was an older friend and a guiding reference in my early years. Ramon and Javi, friends since university, have spent years courageously battling cancer and remain a true source of inspiration and resilience for me. Along with many relatives touched by this disease, they are my reason for riding."


**Sheila Faulcon, senior HR coordinator**


Sheila is riding for her mother-in-law, who is courageously battling[multiple myeloma](https://www.bms.com/medical-resources/disease-information/multiple-myeloma-at-a-glance.html) , and for her sisters-in-law, both cancer survivors. "Cancer has touched my life in too many ways, and this ride is my way of honoring them all."


## Why it matters


The V Foundation for Cancer Research was founded in 1993 by ESPN and the late Jim Valvano. To date, it has funded more than $500 million in cancer research grants across North America through a rigorous, competitive process. Because the V Foundation uses an endowment to cover administrative costs, 100% of direct donations goes to cancer research and programs.


When Gale Force 5 reached Kansas City, they completed their leg of the relay, but the impact of the ride extended beyond the final mile. Every rider had a different story, yet they shared one purpose: helping advance cancer research for the patients, families and communities who depend on it. For Gale Force 5, the journey was always about more than miles.
